Why we stopped billing by the hour, and never looked back.

When we started Fernway Studio, we charged hourly, like every agency does.

Clients were frustrated. So were we. Trust was eroding.

So in 2024, we made a bold decision. One fixed price: KES 450,000 per Shopify store. Period.

It changed everything.

Clients know exactly what they're paying. We work smarter, not longer. Relationships run on trust, not timesheets.

Since then, we've launched 31 stores. Only 2 went over our 6-week timeline.

Pricing isn't just a number. It's a promise.

Founders, how do you price your services? Tell me in the comments.

1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we promised it would always be free for open source. People told us we were crazy. "How will you make money?" they asked.

Today we run on 1,200 repositories. About 900 of them are open source.

Here's what stopped me cold. Across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test. One in seven. That's countless hours of your time burned on red builds that were never real failures.

Open source didn't just hand us users. It handed us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers. We shipped it on November 12.

Giving back isn't charity. It's strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

We built a beautiful app. Nobody used it.

When we launched Rotaship, we were proud of our sleek mobile app. We assumed restaurant staff would love it.

They didn't. Only 12% of staff even opened it in the first month.

That stung. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding another one.

Here's what we learned: restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025, we made a tough call. We moved everything into WhatsApp.

The results: 140 outlets. Median reply time to shift messages: under 20 minutes.

Meet your users where they already are. Don't make them come to you.

Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love.

#ProductManagement #Indonesia #StartupLessons #UserExperience

Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline.

Let me explain.

5 months in, they walked away. It stung. A lot.

But here's the thing: failure isn't the opposite of success. It's part of it.

Why did they leave? They'd heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were.

So we listened. We learned. We built.

We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. That work changed more than our product. It changed how we think about our customers.

Today we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields.

Your biggest setback can become your biggest breakthrough. Lean into the hard feedback. Your customers are telling you what to build. You just have to listen.

What's a loss that shaped your company?

#Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth

After 11 years in a clinic, I walked away. Here's why.

I've always loved being a vet. But something kept breaking my heart. Day after day, I'd see anxious pets so terrified that we had to sedate them just to examine them. I knew there had to be a better way.

So in 2023, I took the leap and founded Doorstep Vet. The idea was simple yet powerful: bring compassionate, high-quality care to pets in the one place they feel safest, their own home.

Today, our team of 4 vets does around 30 home visits a week. And every single one is a reminder of why we do this. Calmer pets. Happier owners. Better medicine.

Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is follow your heart.

#Veterinary #PetCare #Melbourne #Entrepreneurship #FollowYourPassion

We raised our prices by 50%. Here's what happened.

In September, we made one of the scariest calls in Tabwise's history: raising our price from $8 to $12 per user per month.

Why? Our support costs per customer had doubled since launch. So we faced a choice: cut quality, or charge what we're actually worth.

We chose value.

But we weren't going to punish loyal customers for it. Every existing customer kept their $8 price for 12 months.

The result?

Only 2 out of 140 customers churned in the following 2 months.

Two.

Here's the lesson: your customers aren't paying for software. They're paying for outcomes. Price accordingly, and don't be afraid to.

Founders, when did you last raise your prices?

#SaaS #Pricing #StartupLessons #Growth #B2B

Hardware is hard. Here's our story.

Our very first production run at Shelfwise didn't go as planned. 400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact.

As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. But that's not who we are. We made the call to recall and replace every single one of those 400 labels, at our own cost. It set us back about $7,000. Painful? Absolutely. Worth it? 100%.

Because trust is everything.

We didn't stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. Since then, we've had zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

Mistakes don't define you. How you respond to them does. To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.

#Hardware #Startups #Manufacturing #Leadership #Integrity

3 days. That's how long one spindle failure shut down our line.
